findings.claim: Page orientation counting in recover_vertical_texts only treats line direction (0,1) as vertical; a line with direction (0,-1) (bottom-to-top vertical text) is counted as neither vertical nor horizontal.
findings.impact: On a page whose vertical text runs bottom-to-top, the vertical count can stay at zero, so the page is never treated as predominantly vertical and the edge-line/Markdown assembly is kept (I2 branch choice may be wrong). The mixed-page path still appends LTTextBoxVertical boxes, so text is usually recovered, but the predominance rule is not applied as specified.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/extractors/pdf.py:110-113 tests abs(x)<=0.01 and abs(y-1)<=0.01 for the vertical count and abs(x-1)<=0.01 and abs(y)<=0.01 for the horizontal count; a y of -1 matches neither branch. Direction sign convention taken from PyMuPDF knowledge, not from the repository's tests.
findings.repro: not_reproduced: static reading only; no PDF with bottom-to-top vertical text was available to run.

bucket_proposal.reason: In-scope orientation classification defect in normal use, not dependent on crafted input; severity low because the mixed-page path still recovers text.

findings.proposed_fix: Count both (0,1) and (0,-1) as vertical, e.g. abs(x) <= 0.01 and abs(abs(y) - 1) <= 0.01, and add a fixture with bottom-to-top vertical text.

findings.claim: In _extract_with_pymupdf4llm, if fitz.open(path) fails, the vertical recovery step is silently skipped and the page texts from pymupdf4llm/pdfminer-less edge assembly are returned as a successful result.
findings.impact: Vertical boxes are silently absent from indexed text for that document, with no warning and no failure, which can break I1 for such files. Probability is low because pymupdf4llm opens the same file.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/extractors/pdf.py:283-291: except Exception sets document = None, and the recover_vertical_texts call runs only if document is not None; no logger call on this branch.
findings.repro: not_reproduced: requires a PDF that pymupdf4llm reads but fitz.open rejects; not constructed.

bucket_proposal.reason: Silent pass of a failed vertical step in normal use; the spec requires failure to be visible rather than a successful result.

findings.proposed_fix: Log a warning and raise VerticalTextError when fitz.open fails on a page that needs recovery, or treat it the same as a recovery exception.

specification_compliance: No reader finding was listed, so no finding was verified. I read the vertical recovery and the document-text read path at commit 282ae06b and checked the PYMUPDF_LOCK usage and the VerticalTextError propagation. I did not find a spec violation that was not already covered by the two verifier findings above.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Bottom-to-top vertical text (PyMuPDF line direction (0,-1)) has no defined orientation handling; the spec and code are silent on it.
A failed fitz.open in the indexing path skips vertical recovery without a log entry.
regression_risks: Changing the orientation test in pdf.py:110-113 changes which pages take the predominantly-vertical replacement path, so existing indexed chunks for such pages would change on the next rules-version reset.
test_coverage: Not checked: the test files for the PDF extractor and document reader were not read, so I cannot say whether bottom-to-top text or the fitz.open failure path is covered. No tests were run; my tools do not allow it.
not_verified: No tests were run, and no PDF fixtures were executed.
_normalise and _is_contained helper bodies were not read, so the containment rule for mixed pages (I2) was not verified.
The document-text endpoint's handling of VerticalTextError (I5 read failure) was not traced beyond the raise sites.
PyMuPDF line direction sign convention for (0,-1) was taken from library knowledge, not from a repository source.
The 500-page cap, the PYMUPDF_LOCK timeout path (I8) and the citation recomputation (I9) were only partly read.
